examples: a migration giving a column a new name while the old code still reads it
not_for: single-file configuration edits with no ordering

options.definition: a rollout, migration, or rollback step can break dependents or land half-applied
rollout order, rollback, and migration checks are explicit and tested

examples: a renamed command whose reference page still shows the old words
not_for: internal notes nobody reads to use the change

options.definition: the change needs a document, example, or help text updated beside it
every document, example, and help text the change touches is updated

examples: a new command with no entry in the command list agents read
not_for: human-only surfaces, which agents never operate

options.definition: a capability an agent must use is undiscoverable, undescribed, or misdescribed
each capability ships its description, schema, and an example that works

examples: a new script ignoring the repository's ban on network calls in hooks
not_for: rules that exist as checks; those block on their own

options.definition: the change breaks a rule written only in prose: instructions, decisions, or conventions
the change fits the written rules, or carries its exception record

examples: a second way to load configuration beside the established loader
not_for: brand-new ground with no pattern to follow

options.definition: the change departs from an established pattern with no decision record
the change follows the pattern, or records why it does not

examples: three new exported helpers where one private function would do
not_for: surfaces the card explicitly asks to grow

options.definition: the change widens what others must support: new public names with no need shown
each new public name is needed and minimal

examples: a new loader module imported by one test helper
not_for: a second caller arriving in the same change

options.definition: a new helper, layer, or option serves exactly one caller, adding indirection for nothing
each abstraction has the callers that justify it, or stays inline

examples: a public setter added so a test can place state
not_for: seams the design documents for extension

options.definition: production code exists only to serve tests: hooks, backdoors, or test-only branches
tests reach production through its real surface

examples: three callers of one function returning three different fallbacks
not_for: sites the shared handler cannot reach

options.definition: each call site handles errors its own way instead of the shared one
errors flow through the one shared result or handler

examples: a storage helper invoking a handler through a callback the handler passed down
not_for: helpers both layers share by design

options.definition: a lower layer calls into an upper one at runtime
runtime calls point down the layers like the imports do

examples: a workers count read from an option that no command defines
not_for: reserved flags held for a planned use

options.definition: a flag, option, or setting exists that no caller can set or reach
each flag is set somewhere the tests cover

examples: a comment promising retries above code that tries once
not_for: aspirational roadmap notes, marked as such

options.definition: a comment, docstring, or message describes behavior the code beside it does not have
each comment matches the code it stands beside
